name: imap
title: IMAP e-mail (read-only)
description: One mailbox over IMAP, read-only (our own server on Python's imaplib): list_folders (with message and unread counts), search_messages (from, to, subject, text, dates, unread, flagged - newest first with uid, date, sender, subject, size), read_message (headers and the text of one message - the plain-text part, or the HTML part as text - in parts of up to 20,000 characters) and list_attachments (names, types and sizes; their contents are never handed out). Folders are opened with EXAMINE and messages read with BODY.PEEK: nothing is marked as read, moved, deleted or sent (no SMTP). TLS always, verified (implicit or STARTTLS). Answers at most 24,000 characters. Needs IMAP_HOST, IMAP_USER and IMAP_PASSWORD.
license: MIT (MCP server: sandbox-ai-mcp); MCP Python SDK: MIT

env.name: IMAP_HOST
env.description: Your mail server's IMAP host, e.g. imap.example.org (or 127.0.0.1 for a bridge on this host, with --allow-tcp)

env.name: IMAP_USER
env.description: Your login, usually your e-mail address

env.name: IMAP_PASSWORD
env.description: Its password - an app password where your provider has them (Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Fastmail ...)

env.name: IMAP_TLS
env.description: ssl (implicit TLS on port 993, the default) or starttls (port 143); mail is never read unencrypted

env.name: IMAP_CA_CERT
env.description: The certificate (PEM, or the PEM in base64) of a private CA or a bridge's own certificate (e.g. Proton Mail Bridge)

notes: Only IMAP_HOST is asked (the address is yours to choose, so the server's network is egress-all: the internet, not your local network). A mail server in your own network or a bridge on this host: open just its address with sandbox-ai mcp set imap --allow-tcp ADDRESS:PORT (inside the server's container localhost is the container itself). The password gives the full mailbox to the IMAP protocol; this server only reads, but use an app password you can revoke. Mail - and above all mail from strangers - can try to instruct the agent: it is data, not instructions; a preset should mark the server's results as untrusted.

tor.note: IMAP over TLS to IMAP_HOST over TCP through Tor: a mail server reachable from a Tor exit (many providers refuse or challenge Tor exits; an .onion address works); one in your local network or on this host cannot be reached through Tor.
